articles.description: There is cynicism and jealousy but one of County’s top scorers is 39 as club try to climb leagues again after tumbling It was a vidiprinter moment worthy of a double take. Ross County 1 Cove Rangers 1 (Keir 52). Would Cove, scrapping for survival in Scottish League One, put an unlikely end last Saturday to the most emphatic run in British senior football? Don’t be silly, retorted County; four goals in the closing 17 minutes extended the Dingwall side’s goal difference to plus 45 (for 56, against 11). Played 16, won 14, drawn two. There is as much chance of Mike McCarthy settling down for Christmas dinner with Aaron Rodgers as County missing out on promotion back to Scotland’s second tier. Taking in cup competitions they have scored 102 goals this season. Assessment from the captain, Brian Graham, of a frankly irrelevant loss on penalties to Stenhousemuir in the Challenge Cup epitomises the County approach. “We should have been five- or six-nil up at half-time,” an irked Graham says. “That shows the standards we have set. We lost a dubious goal, which shouldn’t have stood.” Earlier in that competition County whacked 14 past a Hearts youth side before defeating a Celtic B team including two Chelsea loanees and a £3m midfielder. articles.title: Liam Delap’s struggles are symbolic of damaging Chelsea churn
articles.dek: The constant turnover of players and staff has made consistency an elusive quality at Stamford Bridge Liam Delap came and went. He joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025…
articles.description: The constant turnover of players and staff has made consistency an elusive quality at Stamford Bridge Liam Delap came and went. He joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025 and was hailed by Enzo Maresca as the next Harry Kane. Fast forward a year, though, and there was no chance of Delap joining Kane in England’s World Cup squad. The striker’s form was miserable and the only surprise was that Chelsea made a profit when they sold him to Nottingham Forest for £50m last summer. On one level it looks like good business. Delap’s only season at Stamford Bridge featured one serious hamstring injury, one league goal, one ridiculous red card and not much else. Analysts at other clubs rated him at Ipswich and felt Chelsea was the wrong fit for his direct style of play. The mistake was less the decision not to give Delap another season, no matter the worries over cover for João Pedro, more the call to sign him in the first place. Continue reading...

articles.title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
articles.dek: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to…
articles.description: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game – and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory – was turned on its head after Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser. The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil – who made up for scoring an own goal in Saturday’s defeat by Coventry capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. Despite Yéremy Pino’s saved penalty in stoppage time and a number of other chances that were squandered, Dean Henderson pulled off a stunning late save to seal the victory and revive Palace’s Europa League campaign. Suddenly Palace have hope where there appeared to be none and the Premier League’s bottom side will head into Sunday’s crucial showdown with Hull with a spring in their step. Continue reading...
